title: Sales Expectations and Machine Removal Notice Under the Vending Services Program
content:
Four figures printed against each programme of the Vending Services Program state what the estate is expected to sell and how long a machine that falls short is given: the monthly sales a machine must make to stay on site, the months of sales below that minimum before the machine is reviewed for removal, the calendar days of notice given before an underperforming machine is removed, and the annual estate sales the programme is written against.

| Programme | Monthly sales a machine must make to stay on site | Months below the minimum before a review | Calendar days of notice before removal | Annual estate sales the programme is written against |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Single Machine Snack Service | 260.00 | 6 | 30 | 3800.00 |
| Snack & Cold Beverage Bank | 340.00 | 6 | 30 | 10200.00 |
| Combination Vending Bank | 480.00 | 4 | 45 | 25200.00 |
| Fresh Food Vending Service | 620.00 | 4 | 45 | 43200.00 |
| Campus Vending Network Service | 540.00 | 3 | 60 | 138000.00 |
| Managed Vending & Kiosk Service | 780.00 | 3 | 60 | 93600.00 |

All money figures are in US dollars. The first figure is stated for one machine in one month; the last is stated for the whole estate over a year. The review count is a whole number of months, and the removal notice is in calendar days.

### Machine figures and estate figures distinguished

The monthly minimum and the annual figure are not two views of the same number and neither is derived from the other. The monthly minimum is read machine by machine: on the Campus Vending Network Service it is 540.00 of sales on a machine in a month. The annual figure is the sales the whole estate is written against for the year: on the same programme it is 138000.00. A machine's own monthly sales are therefore measured against the first figure alone.

### How long a shortfall runs before the notice

The review count and the removal notice also answer different questions. The review count is a number of months of sales below the machine minimum, and it shortens as the programme grows, standing at 6 months on the two smallest programmes, 4 on the Combination Vending Bank and the Fresh Food Vending Service, and 3 on the two largest. The removal notice is a number of calendar days and lengthens across the same span, from 30 days to 60. On the Fresh Food Vending Service the two figures are 4 months and 45 calendar days.
